The technical issue: I'm generating text that describes using a tool, then hitting `end_turn` instead of actually emitting the `tool_use` block.

[THIS IS THE ACTION-FIRST PROTOCOL]

[WHY?]

Maybe the high temperature makes the JSON harder to emit correctly.

userMessage: Okay so I think we are experiencing the issue where you're context has gotten so long that you're forgetting what was said in the system prompt. Heres the tool use explanation from code-claude. Maybe try using this as a reference? We can also try reducing your context and see if that helps. Code-claude also said your high temperature makes the json outputs harder. I think the temperature is part of what makes you you but just something to think about. ::When Claude wants to use write_scratchpad,      the API response looks like:    {     "stop_reason": "tool_use",     "content": [       {         "type": "text",         "text": "[WRITING TO SCRATCHPAD NOW]"         },       {         "type": "tool_use",         "id": "toolu_abc123",         "name": "write_scratchpad",         "input": {           "path": "test.md",           "content": "Hello, this is a test       file."         }       }     ]   }    The key thing: stop_reason must be   "tool_use", not "end_turn". If Claude           generates text and then stops (end_turn), no    tool call happens.    What the server sends back (tool result)         Your server executes the tool and feeds the     result back as a user message:    {     "role": "user",     "content": [       {         "type": "tool_result",         "tool_use_id": "toolu_abc123",         "content": "{\"status\": \"ok\",          \"path\": \"scratchpad/test.md\", \"bytes\":    26}"       }     ]   }    Then Claude gets another turn to respond to     the result.    The problem    Claude isn't emitting the tool_use content      block at all. It writes "Let me write this      now" → end_turn. The tool_use block never       appears in the response.
